Master algorithms through intelligent guidance, progressive hints, and pattern recognition training—not just copy-pasting solutions. Features: Mock interviews, code review, multi-language support (Python, Java, C++, JS, Go). Learn to think like a senior engineer. 🥋

Karan Bansal

I build open-source tools for AI coding agents and write about what I learn from building and using AI systems.

Start here

  • Understand AI: AI Dojo has free explainers and exercises on how AI systems work, where they help, and where they fall short.
  • Use Claude Code tooling: Claude Code Hooks provides installable hooks for secret protection, Git safety, cost visibility, and observability. These are guardrails, not a sandbox. Selected as a tool demo for Black Hat Europe 2026 Arsenal.
  • Understand cache costs: Cache Tax estimates the rewrite cost before a cold send and can keep selected sessions warm during breaks. Warming costs tokens; estimates use API-equivalent prices, not extra subscription charges.
  • Compare mods: Awesome Claude Code Mods is a catalogue of community mods, with scan results showing what each one can access. The scan is a static check of the source, not a safety rating.
  • File an Indian tax return: itr-wala is a skill for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini that prepares an Indian income tax return from your terminal. Tested code does the tax math, not the model. You pay, submit, and e-verify yourself, and it is not professional tax advice.
  • Read Reddit from an AI assistant: Reddit MCP Buddy is an MCP server for browsing and searching Reddit. It works only with Reddit API credentials that Reddit has already approved; Reddit no longer accepts new requests.
  • Read or watch: Writing and talks on AI systems, coding agents, and agent security.

Hi. You must be a rare species if you're reading my bio 😆

My name is Daniel Nguyen. I've been a product engineer for more than 15 years.

Then one day, I discovered Indie Hacking and find it fascinating.

I quit my cushy job to start building in public.

My first product was KTool.io, a tool to send articles & newsletters to Kindle.

I'm half blind, and so I started KTool as a way to offload reading to the Kindle as much as possible.

After 1 year, I didn't find a good way to grow it to ramen profitability, so I decided to learn more about generative AI & OpenAI API, hopefully to find a good freelance gig.

I did land a couple of interesting gigs, but what more interesting is I found a new product idea: BoltAI - a better way to use OpenAI & other AI services on macOS.

I started it purely to learn more about SwiftUI development & OpenAI app development (the so called "AI wrapper")

It's now my top revenue generating product ($500K+).

During building BoltAI, one customer asked about the ability to chat with PDF natively on Mac (another "AI wrapper" idea), I find it interesting and so I decided to build it.

PDF Pals recently reached 1000+ paid customers.

And finally, I build ShotSolve and Oh One Pro as a lead magnet for BoltAI (engineering as marketing, or side project marketing)

It was welcomed by many mac users and so far, has brought many qualified leads to BoltAI. Alright, enough about me. What's about you?

Do you plan to build something cool in 2026?
